subject: math

objective.text: Use place value to round numbers to any place without a number line.

explanations.title: Use the midpoint
explanations.text: Find the two endpoints. Find the midpoint. If the number is less than the midpoint, round down. If it is more, round up.

explanations.title: Round in your head
explanations.text: Without a number line, find the endpoints and the midpoint with mental math. Then compare the number with the midpoint.

explanations.title: Round to any place
explanations.text: One number can be rounded to any place. A smaller unit gives a closer estimate.

explanations.title: Multiply units
explanations.text: 6 ones times 1 ten is 6 tens. 6 tens times 1 ten is 6 hundreds, not 6 tens.

examples.title: Round 4,333
examples.text: 4,333 is between 4,000 and 5,000. The midpoint is 4,500. 4,333 is less than 4,500, so it rounds to 4,000.

examples.title: Round 65,600 to the nearest ten thousand
examples.text: 65,600 is between 60,000 and 70,000. The midpoint is 65,000. 65,600 is more than 65,000, so it rounds to 70,000.

examples.title: Round 147,591 to different places
examples.text: Nearest hundred thousand: 100,000. Ten thousand: 150,000. Thousand: 148,000. Hundred: 147,600. Ten: 147,590.

hints.text: Multiply the numbers. Then name the new unit.
Find the unit below and the unit above the number.
Find the two endpoints and the midpoint. Compare the number with the midpoint.
Round both numbers first. Then subtract the rounded numbers.
The midpoint is half of one unit above the lower endpoint.
Is the number more or less than the midpoint?
Look at which place the headline number is rounded to.
Round each number to its largest place. Then subtract.
Think of the least and greatest numbers that round to this number.
Compare each rounded number with the real number. Which is closer?

misconceptions.label: Keeps the same unit when multiplying by a ten
misconceptions.description: The child thinks 6 tens times 1 ten is 6 tens.
detection_signals: says 6 tens when multiplying 6 tens by 1 ten
misconceptions.response_text: 6 ones times 1 ten is 6 tens. So 6 tens times 1 ten is 6 hundreds.

assets_required.why_this_method: The lesson uses a hand-drawn vertical number line. The child cannot draw it.
assets_required.description: A vertical number line with a lower endpoint, an upper endpoint and a midpoint. The child picks a place, enters a number and can show or hide the line to practice rounding in their head.
must_show_exactly: A vertical line with the lower endpoint at the bottom and the upper endpoint at the top
A midpoint mark with its value
A marker for the chosen number
A text box for a number up to 999,999
A choice of place: ten, hundred, thousand, ten thousand, hundred thousand
A show or hide switch for the line
states_or_frames: A number exactly at the midpoint
assets_required.interaction: Child picks a place and enters a number. The line shows endpoints and midpoint and marks the number. The child picks the nearer endpoint.
assets_required.alt_text: A vertical number line with two endpoints, a midpoint and a marked number.
assets_required.generation_caption: A clean vertical number line with two labeled endpoints, a labeled midpoint, and one marked point. [Build by code]
assets_required.review_notes: Source number lines are drawn by the teacher. Build from the printed values.
